decision.explanation: The sixth roots of unity are e^{2πik/6} for k=0,...,5: six points on the unit circle at angles 0°, 60°, 120°, 180°, 240°, and 300°. Diagram b shows exactly these points.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Which of the following diagrams shows all the $6$th roots of unity?
after.worked_solution:
Geometrically, the $6$th roots of unity have the following properties:

- all of them lie on the unit circle centered in the origin,

- one of the roots is $1,$ corresponding to the point $(1,0)$ on the complex plane,

- the roots form a regular hexagon (regular $6$-sided polygon).

Therefore, the correct answer is the following:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14043589/assets/923d1a1b87833551ae6c451f15a6b5d8bdd75623e8d5c20e86357894bc24683d.png)

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14043589/assets/91f4aac82208a2801652c9112f58518e1abc89ed4313601a60f7c183b7757f70.png)

Find the $10$th root of unity highlighted in the diagram above.
after.worked_solution:
The $n$th roots of unity lie at the vertices of a regular $n$-gon inscribed inside the unit circle in the complex plane. One of the vertices of this regular $n$-gon must lie at the point $(1,0).$

First, we express the complex number $1$ in the form $r{e}^{\text{i}\theta }.$ Notice that $|1|=1$ and $\operatorname{arg}⁡(1)=0.$ Hence, 

$$
1={e}^{\text{i}(0+2k\pi )}={e}^{2k\pi \text{i}},
$$

where $k$ is an integer. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{10}={e}^{2k\pi \text{i}}\,⟹\,z=({e}^{2k\pi \text{i}})^{1/10}={e}^{k\pi \text{i}/5}.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the index $k$ of our root of unity, we enumerate the roots in the diagram counter-clockwise, starting with the root at $(1,0)$ corresponding to $k=0,$ as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14043589/assets/d0fc6866d4bb06ec6cbf20bb719faf722ec3c1efe3fba03e413f51dc1c827e71.png)

 

So, the required root corresponds to $k=8.$ Substituting this into the expression for roots, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}_{8}={e}^{(8)\pi \text{i}/5}={e}^{8\pi \text{i}/5}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

Find the 10th root of unity highlighted in the diagram above.

a
e19πi/10
b
e17πi/10
c
e9πi/5
d
e8πi/5
e
e7πi/5
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The nth roots of unity lie at the vertices of a regular n-gon inscribed inside the unit circle in the complex plane. One of the vertices of this regular n-gon must lie at the point (1,0).

First, we express the complex number 1 in the form reiθ. Notice that |1|=1 and arg⁡(1)=0. Hence,

1=ei(0+2kπ)=e2kπi,

where k is an integer. So, we have

z10=e2kπi⟹z=(e2kπi)1/10=ekπi/5.

To find the index k of our root of unity, we enumerate the roots in the diagram counter-clockwise, starting with the root at (1,0) corresponding to k=0, as shown below.

So, the required root corresponds to k=8. Substituting this into the expression for roots, we obtain the following:

z8=e(8)πi/5=e8πi/5

verification.explanation: The highlighted root has index k=8, counting counterclockwise from (1,0). Thus z=e^{2πi(8)/10}=e^{8πi/5}, matching option d and the revealed solution.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14043589/assets/91f4aac82208a2801652c9112f58518e1abc89ed4313601a60f7c183b7757f70.png)

Find the $10$th root of unity highlighted in the diagram above.
content.worked_solution:
The $n$th roots of unity lie at the vertices of a regular $n$-gon inscribed inside the unit circle in the complex plane. One of the vertices of this regular $n$-gon must lie at the point $(1,0).$

First, we express the complex number $1$ in the form $r{e}^{\text{i}\theta }.$ Notice that $|1|=1$ and $\operatorname{arg}⁡(1)=0.$ Hence, 

$$
1={e}^{\text{i}(0+2k\pi )}={e}^{2k\pi \text{i}},
$$

where $k$ is an integer. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{10}={e}^{2k\pi \text{i}}\,⟹\,z=({e}^{2k\pi \text{i}})^{1/10}={e}^{k\pi \text{i}/5}.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the index $k$ of our root of unity, we enumerate the roots in the diagram counter-clockwise, starting with the root at $(1,0)$ corresponding to $k=0,$ as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14043589/assets/d0fc6866d4bb06ec6cbf20bb719faf722ec3c1efe3fba03e413f51dc1c827e71.png)

 

So, the required root corresponds to $k=8.$ Substituting this into the expression for roots, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}_{8}={e}^{(8)\pi \text{i}/5}={e}^{8\pi \text{i}/5}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

Find the 8th root of unity highlighted in the diagram above.

a
e7πi/4
b
e11πi/8
c
e5πi/4
d
e3πi/2
e
e9πi/8
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The nth roots of unity lie at the vertices of a regular n-gon inscribed inside the unit circle in the complex plane. One of the vertices of this regular n-gon must lie at the point (1,0).

First, we express the complex number 1 in the form reiθ. Notice that |1|=1 and arg⁡(1)=0. Hence,

1=ei(0+2kπ)=e2kπi,

where k is an integer. So, we have

z8=e2kπi⟹z=(e2kπi)1/8=ekπi/4.

To find the index k of our root of unity, we enumerate the roots in the diagram counter-clockwise, starting with the root at (1,0) corresponding to k=0, as shown below.

So, the required root corresponds to k=5. Substituting this into the expression for roots, we obtain the following:

z5=e(5)πi/4=e5πi/4

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14043589/assets/ff773f71725cdd3c81f3100623f3b4cc86f3096a3d7f59d14b6943ffa5f11a2b.png)

Find the $8$th root of unity highlighted in the diagram above.
content.worked_solution:
The $n$th roots of unity lie at the vertices of a regular $n$-gon inscribed inside the unit circle in the complex plane. One of the vertices of this regular $n$-gon must lie at the point $(1,0).$

First, we express the complex number $1$ in the form $r{e}^{\text{i}\theta }.$ Notice that $|1|=1$ and $\operatorname{arg}⁡(1)=0.$ Hence, 

$$
1={e}^{\text{i}(0+2k\pi )}={e}^{2k\pi \text{i}},
$$

where $k$ is an integer. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{8}={e}^{2k\pi \text{i}}\,⟹\,z=({e}^{2k\pi \text{i}})^{1/8}={e}^{k\pi \text{i}/4}.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the index $k$ of our root of unity, we enumerate the roots in the diagram counter-clockwise, starting with the root at $(1,0)$ corresponding to $k=0,$ as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14043589/assets/9bbdc0b5be31f5c54fdf3390ec62d2130f528d2807305167f94a5612e39d67de.png)

 

So, the required root corresponds to $k=5.$ Substituting this into the expression for roots, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}_{5}={e}^{(5)\pi \text{i}/4}={e}^{5\pi \text{i}/4}\end{aligned}
$$
